newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times front page - March 13.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times front page - March 13.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following stories on its front page Thursday:

* Congress has begun searching for a way to rebuke Mexico for failures in its drug-fighting efforts without disturbing the country's economy. Meanwhile, the White House said President Clinton could veto a House bill overturning his recent finding that Mexico is cooperating in the drug war.

* A Federal probe into possible efforts by China to influence American politicians began early last year when the National Security Agency secretly monitored communications between Beijing and Chinese officials in the U.S.
* As judges and legislators mull the theoretical aspects of doctor-assisted suicides, physicians are faced with making real and agonizing decisions with suffering patients.

* News Analysis: Broadcasters have begun fighting a call for them to give political candidates free air time, saying that such a move would violate their First and Fifth Amendment rights and potentially bore viewers.

* Zairean rebels have never been closer to reaching the two goals of their insurgency - the overthrow of longtime dictator Mobutu Sese Seko and the break-up of concentrations of Hutu refugees in their country.

* Since its start in 1973, Alaska's Iditarod sled-dog race has become the Mardi Gras of the Arctic, a festival that is entrenched in the state's culture and identity and that draws corporate sponsors and thousands of revelers and volunteers.
* The Nigerian Government charged celebrated playwright and Nobel laureate Wole Soyinka and 11 other dissidents with treason after a series of bombings at army sites.
